Work in your own git worktree of the Wisp plugins repo (orin-dx/wisp-plugins). First `/usr/bin/git fetch -q origin` (network: dangerouslyDisableSandbox true) then `/usr/bin/git merge --no-edit origin/feat/gate-round-limits`. Read AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/adr/README.md, docs/architecture-assumptions.md, docs/evaluations/frontend-design/IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md (all sections, especially "Evidence review and ADR 015", "ADR evidence"), docs/evaluations/frontend-design/ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md and shared/references/architecture/decision-records.md.

Task: write ONE design document, docs/design/agent-native-architecture.md, that applies "design it twice" to the plugin architecture and proposes how to get there. Docs only: change no plugin, agent, skill or schema.

Context the owner established (treat as given):
- The plugins mirror a human org chart (handoff documents, sign-off gates, role-named agents). Evidence: value came from first-round independent checks against code or a build; repeated rounds, duplicate reviews of the same draft, per-commit review and mutation on logic-free code were waste; no reviewer caught a logic bug; 77% of subagent tokens went to ad hoc forks and general-purpose agents, not plugins; plugin agents mostly ran without their skills (routing failed); resident description text and always-loaded plugins are a cost (TokenEconomizer: pruning unused tools was the largest saving; failed trajectories take about a third of spend).
- Principles: agents are not a team of people, so do not build them one; models were trained on human organizations and reproduce their ceremony, so strategy must be asked for explicitly; humans set direction and agents identify, propose, enforce and deliver within it with decisions at the points that change direction; do not over-prescribe (outcome, constraints, evidence bar; must-hold rules go in deterministic checks); autonomy and independent review scale with reversibility and blast radius; humans get artifacts only at the edges (brief and decision cards in; diff or render, evidence, a list of what was not verified, and the changelog or PR out); keep independent verification only where a confident mistake is costly or irreversible; the spec for agents is something a machine can check.
- Ousterhout: over-specialization and conjoined pieces that must be read together should be joined; deep modules over many shallow ones; but do not go to one mega-agent.

Document shape (follow the record's own consistency: scannable, bullets, bold lead-ins, short; no word target, the decision sets the length):
1. **Goal and constraints** (what the architecture must achieve for the owner and for agents).
2. **Three structurally different architectures**, each with: shape, who does what, what artifacts humans see, how checks work, what it removes, cost and risk, what evidence supports and contradicts it. A: today's plugins trimmed (what we have after ADR 015 and the routing guard). B: a deep core: a risk-aware work skill, one full-context worker, an independent verifier, edge artifacts, loaded-on-demand specialization references. C: a single agent plus hooks and executable evidence only. Do not strawman any of them.
3. **The strategic layer** (applies to B and to a trimmed A): a guided loop of identify, propose options (design twice), the owner decides via decision cards, encode the answer as a guardrail or check, deliver, monitor; what triggers it (cadence, repeated fixes in one area, an assumption going stale, duplicated work); what it may do unasked and what needs the owner, by reversibility.
4. **Comparison** table against the constraints, and a **recommendation** with confidence and what would change it.
5. **How to decide**: the paired fix-task sequence measurement (docs/evaluation-runbook.md) as the test between A, B and C, with the metrics and a first small experiment that could run next week.
6. **Open questions for the owner.**

State evidence honestly, with its limits (one author, few projects, single runs). Link to existing records instead of restating them. This is a proposal, not a decision; do not write an ADR.

Run `just check` and judge by exit code (the new doc must not break link or style checks). Commit locally with `/usr/bin/git add -A` then a separate `/usr/bin/git commit` with dangerouslyDisableSandbox true (GPG signing; approved), message ending with `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01SGj1qDtVs8manZp9LRpuqm`. Use /usr/bin/git for git; avoid the word git in other command text, heredocs and $(...). Do not push. Report your branch and commit, your recommendation, and anything the evidence could not answer.

<system-reminder>
Other agents active in this session, addressable via SendMessage({to: name, message}): main, adr-condense, adr-old, adr-scan, audit-docs, audit-harness, audit-projects, backstory-removal, catch-rate, catch-rate-2, ceremony-navigator, ceremony-readiness, ceremony-versions, evidence-docs, gate-hygiene, measurement, planner, repo-decisions, session-data, skill-routing.
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

1	# Architecture assumptions register
2	
3	Every part of a harness encodes an assumption about what the model cannot do on its own, and those assumptions go stale as models and hosts change. This register records each load-bearing assumption in `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the decision records, the evidence for and against it, and the check that would retire it. Review it when a new model generation ships, when Claude Code or Codex changes how agents, hooks or plugins work, and before a release. First version: 2026-10-20, from `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md` after primary-source verification.
4	
5	Status: **Holds**, **Changing** (a work package is in progress), **Open** (evidence is mixed; a measurement is planned), **Retire** (evidence says drop it).
6	
7	| # | Assumption | Where it lives | Evidence now | Status | Next check |
8	| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
9	| 1 | Context is scarce, so load references on demand | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 1, `<load_first>` blocks | Skills are progressive disclosure natively; Anthropic's context guidance asks for the minimal sufficient information | Holds | Re-read when context-window or compaction behavior changes |
10	| 2 | One agent per cognitive mode | ADR 003, `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 7 | Anthropic recommends splitting by context isolation, not role, and multi-agent runs cost 3 to 15 times a single agent; verifier, adversary and recon splits are justified by independent context | Open | WP-605 classifies each of the 44 agents; WP-601 tests collapsed variants against a no-plugin baseline |
11	| 3 | A byte-identical constitution block is a shared cache prefix | ADR 006 | The block is 6 lines in each agent, so its cost is small; cache prefixes are shared only for the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and directory, with a 5-minute subagent TTL | Open | WP-604 measures sharing; no change unless a net benefit is shown |
12	| 4 | Capability tiers by model and effort | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5 | Effort is a native per-agent control; defaults and semantics differ by model; the Codex tiers were re-chosen by position and are unevaluated | Open | WP-63 sweeps effort at the effort actually run; re-check on each model release |
13	| 5 | JSON schemas are the inter-agent contract | ADR 004 | Portable across harnesses; recorded gate verdicts conform except one rule (summary length) | Holds | Enforce deterministically (WP-602) |
14	| 6 | The `reasoning` scratchpad field is safe | Constitution, 33 of 35 schemas | Documentation names such a field as a refusal trigger; a live probe on Sonnet 5.5 completed normally with the field and refused only a demand for verbatim reasoning; no refusals in 72k+ transcript messages | Holds | `tests/test_reasoning_wording.py` guards the wording; re-run the probe per model generation and on Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Haiku 5.5 (WP-625) |
15	| 7 | Default-fail gates with a retry cap and human escalation (cap was 3; two rounds since ADR 015) | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6 | The cap lived in a prompt and was not enforced: eight specs passed with `retry_count` 4 to 9; the `muse` gate told the agent to emit a verdict value no schema allows (fixed) | Changing | Two rounds since ADR 015 (cap of one retry, enforced by the hook; escalation on a repeated blocker), after evidence that useful catches come in rounds one and two |
16	| 8 | Orchestration is a skill prompt that spawns subagents | Plugin skills | The assistant never invoked the skills (7 Skill calls in 812 transcripts), so agents reachable only through skills never ran; the platform offers workflow scripts that keep state outside the model | Changing | WP-603; Wave 1 makes skills the entry point |
17	| 9 | Work is a sequential pipeline of ten plugins | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 3 | Autonomous runs are getting longer and stage granularity tuned for short horizons goes stale; stages should be elidable | Open | WP-608, WP-18 (mode router) |
18	| 10 | Plans carry exact implementation code | navigator, ADR 009 | Anthropic kept its own planner at high-level design and says over-prescriptive guidance degrades newer models; large plans stalled agents | Open | WP-608: outcome-level plans |
19	| 11 | Verification evidence is text, code and tests | `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4 | Every target harness has a native browser; one study found 44.5% of agent runs never looked at the design screenshots; visible defects shipped past every gate | Changing | WP-607, WP-40, WP-41 |
20	| 12 | Agents are stateless across sessions | no memory design | Decisions were lost between sessions; native memory, persistent plugin data and session search exist | Changing | WP-612, WP-13 |
21	| 13 | Two source trees, one lifecycle contract | `ARCHITECTURE.md` sections 8 to 10 | Codex has its own native plugin format set up in `harnesses/codex/`; Antigravity's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree; Agent Plugins 1.0.0 standardizes a portable core | Holds | WP-610 |
22	| 14 | Humans approve through written artifacts | specs, verdicts | The user asked for rendered examples repeatedly and drawn prototypes exposed defects the gated spec missed | Changing | WP-34, WP-614 |
23	| 15 | Agents use only `model` and `effort` of the host's controls | agent frontmatter | The host also offers `tools`, `maxTurns`, `isolation`, `skills` preload and `memory`; plugin agents ignore `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `permissionMode` | Open | WP-606 |
24	
25	## How to update
26	
27	Add a row when a decision record or architectural section introduces a new assumption. Change a status only with the evidence that moved it, citing a file in `docs/evaluations/` or a dated fact in `docs/verified-facts.md`. When a status becomes **Retire**, open or update the decision record that carries the assumption.

# Decision Records

Decide whether an architectural choice needs a durable record, and write the record so a later reader with no memory of the discussion does not silently reverse it. A record preserves the reason behind a decision, so nobody accepts it blindly or reverses it blindly.

## Write one only when both gates pass

- **Architectural:** the choice sets a boundary, a model, a direction, or a rule that several changes must respect.
- **Expensive to reverse or not obvious from the code:** a reader who sees only the code would plausibly undo it, or undoing it would be costly.

One decision per record. A choice that fails a gate belongs elsewhere.

| Fact | Home |
| :--- | :--- |
| Architecture, model, direction, decision, rejected alternative | Decision record in `docs/adr/` |
| Rule for every session: command, invariant, style, routing | `AGENTS.md` |
| Required behavior | Spec |
| How the system works today | Docs |
| Why one change was made | Commit message |
| Personal preference or correction for one repository | Agent memory, uncommitted |

Agent memory is unshared and goes stale, so a decision never lives only there.

## Goal

A reader two years from now, human or agent, with no memory of the discussion, can see in a minute what was decided, why it was right here, what was rejected and why, what it costs, and when to reconsider it. Everything in a record serves that. Everything else is cheaper to keep elsewhere: measurements and discussion in the evaluation log, changes in the commit or PR.

## Shape

People scan records and look for the same thing in the same place, so the layout is consistent even though the content is not.

- Headings in a fixed order: **Decision**, **Why**, **Rejected**, **Consequences** (with a `Revisit when` trigger), **Evidence** (one line: where the measurements and discussion live).
- Lead with the point. Use short bullets for parallel items (rules, forces, alternatives, costs) and bold lead-ins so a skim finds each. Use a sentence or two of prose only where a causal "because" needs it.
- Say a finding in words; keep a number only when the number is the constraint.
- `Enforced by` when a test, lint, type or hook enforces the decision. A decision a check can enforce should have the check; the record explains why it exists.
- An index line in `docs/adr/README.md` of the form `Do not <X> without a new ADR`, for a decision an agent could undo without noticing.

Let the decision set the shape and the length. A record that grows long usually holds several decisions (split it) or a session log (move the log). Records written before this form keep their form.

## What stays

For each sentence ask whether a reader two years on needs it to understand why the architecture is shaped this way, or to know when to change it. If it only tells how we got here, it belongs elsewhere.

| Belongs in the record | Belongs elsewhere |
| :--- | :--- |
| The decision and its boundary | Measurements, run counts, token figures: the evaluation log |
| Lasting forces and constraints | One-off test dates, "a live run showed": the evaluation log |
| Rejected options and why | Files, tests, versions changed: the commit or PR |
| Costs and the revisit trigger | Open-measurement lists: one `Revisit when` in the record |
| The guardrail | The tour of the investigation: the PR or trail |

The agent writing a record has the session fresh and will want to include all of it. `scripts/check-adr-style.py` warns on session-log markers and on a record long enough to hold several decisions; it never fails, so judgment stays with the writer.

## Prose

Keep the causal "because" and the rejected alternative. Cut narration of the discussion, restated code, and hedging.

## Status and change

Do not rewrite an accepted record's context, decision, or options; the reasoning at the time is what the record preserves. Update its status and links, and fix errors that do not change its meaning. To change a decision, write a new record that supersedes it and mark the old one superseded; the old record stays. Keep the active set small by writing records only for decisions that pass both gates.

## Refutation and disposition

Evidence for a record is the code, spec, or constraint it governs. Before proposing a boundary, read the accepted records for that area. Treat a superseded record as history, not a constraint.

- **Write:** both gates pass and no accepted record covers the choice.
- **Supersede:** the new decision reverses an accepted record; cite it and state what changed.
- **Skip:** the choice is a preference, a routine change, or already obvious from the code; put the reason in the commit message.
- **Coverage gap:** if `docs/adr/` is absent, say so. Absence does not prove that no decision governs the area.

1	# Evaluation runbook
2	
3	How to run the paired design in `docs/evaluation-methodology.md` on real work, for three task kinds. The question each time: does the treatment reduce turns and tokens, and does the first result need less rework? Single-run pilots and anecdotes cannot answer that. Pairs can, within the limits below.
4	
5	`tools/transcript-metrics.py turns`, `agents`, `context` and `gates` measure; `tools/paired-analysis.py compare` and `agreement` analyse. `tests/test_transcript_metrics.py` (`DryRunTests`) runs this pipeline on synthetic sessions.
6	
7	## Before any run
8	
9	1. **Write the task list and the checklists first.** Take 6 to 10 real tasks from the backlog, each with a blinded checklist (see Scoring). Nothing is edited after the first run.
10	2. **Pin everything but the treatment.** Same model id, effort, repo commit, permission mode, and CLAUDE.md and memory. Record plugin versions and dates (methodology rule 10). Start each run in a fresh session from a clean checkout of the repo state.
11	3. **Randomize order.** Flip a coin per task for which arm runs first, so fatigue and your own learning do not fall on one arm. Run each pair on the same day.
12	4. **Run each arm per task once, then repeat** when you can: two to three runs, reduced to the median per task.
13	5. **One person drives, another scores.** The driver answers the agent's questions the same way in both arms (write the answers down on the first run and reuse them). Stop when the driver would accept the result; that is "acceptance".
14	
15	## Capturing a session
16	
17	The transcript is `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-dir>/<session-id>.jsonl` (read only; never copy it into the repo). For each finished run:
18	
19	```
20	python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py turns --file <transcript> --trial task=T1,arm=control,run=1,score=0.7,defects=2 >> trials.jsonl
21	python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py context --match '<project-dir-suffix>$'
22	python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py agents --match '<project-dir-suffix>$'
23	python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py gates <directory holding <spec>-verdict[-n].json>
24	```
25	
26	Add `gate_rounds=N` to `--trial` for the spec task and `ctx_chars=N` from `context`'s total. The `turns` fields: `prompts` (human prompts, the turns to acceptance), `turns` (assistant messages), `tool_calls`, `subagents`, `retries` (a call right after a failure, same tool, changed input; rework signal, defined in the tool docstring), `subagent_tokens` (as reported by subagents, not a bill). `context` is cumulative over the matched sessions, so match one session per run or use a dedicated project directory per arm.
27	
28	Then:
29	
30	```
31	python3 tools/paired-analysis.py compare trials.jsonl --baseline control --metrics score,prompts,turns,retries,subagent_tokens,gate_rounds
32	```
33	
34	## Task kinds
35	
36	### A. Design ideation (muse or sketch against an ad hoc session)
37	
38	- **Statement**: "Explore <N=3> directions for <screen or component> in <repo>. Constraints: <list>. Stop when I can pick one."
39	- **Control**: plain session, no plugin, the same statement. **Treatment**: `muse:sketch` with the plugin installed.
40	- **Fixed**: model, effort, repo commit, design tokens and brief, the driver's selection rule (pick the option meeting the constraints; ties go to the first).
41	- **Primary metrics**: prompts to acceptance, `subagent_tokens`, `context` characters by origin, quality score, and whether the chosen direction survives promotion to a spec without being redone.
42	- **Defects found later**: constraint violations a reviewer finds in the accepted option within one week.
43	
44	### B. Spec drafting and gating (gated pipeline now versus before gate hygiene)
45	
46	- **Statement**: "Draft and gate a spec for <requirement>" with a requirement of fixed text.
47	- **Control**: the plugins at commit `50bdcf1b^` (before the gate-hygiene change), checked out in a separate worktree and loaded as the plugin source. **Treatment**: the plugins at the commit under test. Disable the installed marketplace copy in both so only one version loads, and record the commit in each trial.
48	- **Fixed**: requirement text, model, effort, a prewritten set of answers to clarifying questions, retry cap.
49	- **Primary metrics**: `gate_rounds` (from `gates`), blockers per round, `subagent_tokens` from `agents`, prompts to a passed gate, long summaries and escalations.
50	- **Defects found later**: criteria that a reviewer who has not seen the gate verdicts finds untestable, missing an error case or contradicting the requirement; and spec contradictions raised when the spec is implemented.
51	
52	### C. Changeset and PR text (courier with layered `changeset@3` guidance versus freehand)
53	
54	- **Statement**: "Write the changeset and PR description for this diff" with a stored diff (`gh pr diff <n>` saved outside the repo, or a branch to check out).
55	- **Control**: freehand, no courier skills, no changeset guidance in context. **Treatment**: `courier:changeset` then `courier:pr`.
56	- **Fixed**: diff, repo conventions file and PR template, model, effort.
57	- **Primary metrics**: prompts to acceptance, `retries`, tokens (`agents` plus main-thread `context`), characters of text produced, quality score.
58	- **Defects found later**: a release reader's questions the text did not answer, wrong semver impact, missing limits or breaking-change marks, found by someone who did not write either text.
59	
60	## Scoring
61	
62	A scorer who did not run the sessions scores both outputs **blind**: strip arm names, plugin names and agent-specific markers, and shuffle. The checklist is written before the first run and frozen. Each item is yes, no or not applicable, with a one-line evidence note. Score = yes / (yes + no).
63	
64	```
65	Task: ___  Output id (shuffled): ___  Scorer: ___  Date: ___
66	| # | Checklist item (observable, yes or no)        | Yes/No/NA | Evidence |
67	| 1 | <task-specific, written before the run>        |           |          |
68	Defects found in later review (count, with one line each): ___
69	Score: ___ / ___ = ___     Would accept as-is? yes / no
70	```
71	
72	Calibration: for task kind B and C, have a second scorer (or an LLM judge) score at least 20 items, then run `python3 tools/paired-analysis.py agreement labels.json` with `[{"a": ..., "b": ...}]`. Use an LLM judge only at kappa of about 0.6 or above (convention, not measured). Below that, score by hand.
73	
74	## How many pairs, and what a null shows
75	
76	- The exact Wilcoxon test cannot reach p < 0.05 with fewer than 6 non-tied pairs, whatever the effect. Run **at least 6 pairs per task kind**; aim for 10, with repeats.
77	- With 6 to 10 pairs only large effects (on the order of a third of turns or tokens, or most items flipping in the checklist) can reach significance. A smaller real effect will look like noise.
78	- **A null result shows**: no large effect on that task kind, for that model and effort, on those tasks. **It does not show**: no effect, no effect at other efforts, or no effect on other repositories. Report the pair count, the median relative change with its direction, and the better, worse and tied counts. A consistent direction across tasks at n = 8 (say 7 of 8 better) is evidence worth following up, not proof.
79	- Do not mix kinds. Do not drop a task because the treatment lost. A crashed task is dropped from every arm and counted.
80	- Tag the write-up with `small-sample` and `self-benchmark` where they apply (`docs/evidence-quality.md`).
81	
82	## Results table
83	
84	```
85	| Task kind | Pairs | Prompts (median delta) | Turns | Retries | Subagent tokens | Gate rounds | Score (better/worse/tied) | Defects later | Verdict |
86	| A ideation |  |  |  |  |  | n/a |  |  |  |
87	| B spec gate |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
88	| C changeset/PR |  |  |  |  | n/a |  |  |  |
89	Provenance: model ___, effort ___, plugin commits ___ / ___, repo commit ___, dates ___, runs per task ___, excluded ___.
90	Power note and what would change the conclusion: ___
91	```
92	
93	## Limits
94	
95	Turn counts depend on how the driver answers. Subagent tokens are reported, not billed, and the main thread's tokens are not in them; `context` counts characters, not tokens, and ignores caching. Retries include legitimate progress. Treat the numbers as a comparison between arms on the same driver, not as absolute costs.
96

## What the work found

- **`claude plugin validate plugins/<id>` was a false pass** because the manifests sit at the plugin root. With the generated `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` it validates the manifest, and the repo-only keys (`id`, `consumes`, `produces`) stay in `plugin.json` where Claude Code ignores them.
- **Recorded gate verdicts nearly all conform to their schemas.** 33 of 45 conform; all 12 violations are `verdict_summary` over 300 characters (`VERIFY-3.md` section 5). A hook would have asked for one trim on about 27% of handbacks.
- **`muse` gates mostly emitted `verdict@3`-shaped output** (26 of 36; the other 9 of the 45 files are `scribe` gates) while `muse` documented `verdict@1`, and its prompt told the agent to set `verdict` to `"escalate"`, which no schema allows. WP-02 (done) moved `muse` to `verdict@3` and made escalation an `escalation_required` blocker, as in the other four gates; the validator now checks `muse` against `verdict@3` only.
- **A bug in the validator was found only by real data:** a schema property with a list of types (`["string", "null"]`). It is fixed and has a regression test.
- **The `requirement@1` schema describes `reasoning` as "chain-of-thought during capture".** It is immutable (ADR 004), agents reach it through a file read and not a prompt, so the lint carries a documented exception; a future `requirement@2` should use the "private scratchpad" wording.

## Open items from this work

- The README documents AGY installs through the community `agy-plugins-cli`. Fetched source snippets suggest that tool discovers plugins as top-level repository directories, which would not find plugins under `plugins/`. This is unverified; test an install in an isolated environment before changing the README (WP-622, WP-621).
- The installed plugins use `shared -> ../../shared` symlinks and the Claude marketplace installs from the `plugins/<id>` subdirectory (`git-subdir`). Whether the symlink resolves after install is untested (WP-621).
- The hook is a spike: it needs a plugin `hooks/hooks.json` registration, a decision on how it is distributed (the tool lives outside any plugin directory), and a check against a live gate agent in auto mode before WP-602 builds on it.
- Hook behavior on Claude Code 2.1.292: `onFailure: "block"` needs 2.1.295, so a crashing hook does not block (the validator fails open by design).

The repo's contribution checklist asks for a plugin version bump, a plugin changelog entry and a matching marketplace entry when a plugin's behavior changes, and the version check compares all of them. The planner now says to add no keys outside the schema and to carry the content in `steps`; the final runs also named the schema path in the prompt.
160	
161	Not done: the `plan@1` field descriptions still say "exact code" (a published schema is not edited, ADR 004); a `plan@2` with explicit outcome, signature and test fields is deferred.
162	
163	## Gate rounds (track B, ADR 013)
164	
165	| Finding | Action | Evidence |
166	| :-- | :-- | :-- |
167	| Every spec failed its first gate and blocker counts were non-monotonic (SPEC-001: 18, 5, 6, 0, 0, 2, 0, 6, 2, 3, 2, 8, 3) | Each of the five exit gates now states two output rules, worded the same: round one lists the complete blocker set; a retry cites only unresolved prior blockers or regressions the fix introduced, and any other new issue is a non-blocking `coverage_gaps` entry; every blocker names the criterion, cites quoted text or a location and states the exact change; wording or style issues are notes | `just check` exit 0; `verdict@3` unchanged |
168	| Drafters sent unchecked drafts to the gate | New `shared/references/verification/gate-readiness.md` (blocker shape, rounds, spec checklist) loaded by `muse:drafter` and `scribe:drafter`, with a short inline fallback if the path does not resolve; Codex `author` and `judge` role cards updated | `just check` |
169	| Blocker shape could not be enforced deterministically without false denials | The hook denies only a blocker or coverage gap whose text is whitespace; evidence citing is not checked | `tests/test_handback_validator.py` |
170	
171	Live runs, one run each on Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Code 2.1.311, `claude -p --permission-mode auto --plugin-dir`, working directory outside the repository, `WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE` set). The prompt read a task file asking for one delegation to `<plugin>:exit-gate` with a small spec or finding that had known defects. The trace showed `agent_type` `<plugin>:exit-gate` in all four. Scribe, sentinel and smith were accepted on the first report. Ranger was denied once and accepted on the second; the trace does not record the denial reason, so what the first report broke is unknown. All four returned fail with blockers that gave a criterion or finding id, a location and an exact change; the smith report also listed `missing_mutation_gate` and `unresolved_review` as blockers, and the scribe report flagged the TBD and the vague "gracefully" criterion. These runs were round one only: they confirm the hook fires and the gates produce evidence-citing blockers, not that rounds fall. Nothing here measures the retry rule.
172	
173	Not done: a measured comparison of round counts before and after (needs a paired run of gate, fix and regate, WP-60); passing the prior round's blockers into the gate on retry (the skills do not, so the retry rule depends on the orchestrator); a self-check for `smith:implementer`, `sentinel:verifier` and `ranger` producers; a check that the `shared/...` path resolves from a user's project (see the Courier finding above).
174	
175	## Integration, path resolution and versions
176	
177	| Finding | Action | Evidence |
178	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
179	| Relative `shared/...` paths in agents and skills do not resolve reliably: with `shared` a symlink, a probe skill first tried its own directory and a probe agent first tried the working directory, each costing a failed read; an explicit `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/...` path read on the first try in both | Rewrote 163 references in 66 agent and skill files to the plugin-root form. Codex sources are unchanged because Codex does not substitute the token | Four probe runs (one each, Claude Code 2.1.311, Sonnet 5.5); then `courier:changeset-analyzer` on the Callisto PR 483 diff reported its reference loaded from the full plugin path on the first read |
180	| The gate retry rule needs `retry_count` and the prior blockers as input; no skill passed them | One sentence in the gate-calling skills (muse `component`, scribe `gate-spec`, sentinel `gate`, smith `implement`, ranger `audit`) and the Codex counterparts | `just check` |
181	| Tracks B to E (gate hygiene, measurement, skill routing, planner) ran in parallel worktrees and were merged here | Merged with log-only conflicts resolved by keeping both sides | `just check` exit 0 after each merge |
182	| Nine plugins had changed against `main` with no version or changelog | muse 1.1.0, smith 2.5.0, navigator 2.4.0, scribe 3.5.0, courier 3.1.0; sentinel, ranger, mason, vanguard and weaver patch bumps; ecosystem 4.5.0 | `just versions`, `just check`, `just claude-validate` |
183	
184	Limits: the path finding rests on single probe runs; Antigravity's handling of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in skill and agent text was not tested, and its format shares the authored tree, so confirm it before releasing. The hook-only plugins (sentinel, ranger) are patch bumps although a gate can now deny a report that used to pass; scribe is a minor because its drafter and skills also changed behavior.
185	
186	## Top-tier models removed
187	
188	| Finding | Action | Evidence |
189	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
190	| Two agents (`scribe:arch-auditor`, `scribe:architect`) ran on `claude-fable-5-1`, about twice Opus, and `arch-auditor` runs on every spec; the Codex `judge` role ran on `gpt-6-astra`. The constitution said fable was never for gates or per-finding loops, and no measurement shows either tier catches more | Both scribe agents move to `opus / high`, the constitution drops the fable tier, the Codex `judge` moves to `gpt-6.1-sol / high`; tier tests updated | `just check`. Quality effect unmeasured: run the spec-gating paired comparison in `docs/evaluation-runbook.md` and restore a tier if boundary conflicts or binding verdicts are missed |
191	
192	Codex `author` role: moved from `gpt-6.1-sol` / high to `gpt-6.1-terra` / medium (Terra is about half of Sol's price per token and is positioned for clear writing; the page lists no effort levels for it, so the effort label stays relative). Other roles unchanged. Unmeasured: whether Terra drafts specs, PR text and changesets as well as Sol; run the spec-drafting and courier comparisons in `docs/evaluation-runbook.md`.
193	
194	## Model and effort fit
195	
196	Audit of all 45 agents against the constitution's tiers (haiku/low for mechanical work, sonnet/medium for analysis and execution, opus/high for binding judgment). Two clear mismatches changed: `courier:release-summarizer` sonnet/medium to haiku/low (deterministic aggregation), `scribe:drift-checker` opus/high to sonnet/medium (a diagnostic, not a gate). Left alone pending measurement, in order of likely saving: `ranger:adversary` (one opus call per candidate), `scribe:arch-auditor` (opus on every spec), `sentinel:exit-gate` (maps a verifier report to a verdict without re-reading evidence, so it may not need opus), and whether opus gates need `high` rather than the default effort. Gate quality decides retry rounds, so a cheaper gate that misses more can cost more than it saves; test with the spec-gating comparison in `docs/evaluation-runbook.md` before changing them.
197	
198	## Evidence review and ADR 015
199	
200	Three independent reads (documented evidence; session token data over 1,555 subagent calls and 253M reported tokens in five projects; reviewer catch rate over about 400 runs) agreed the structure is partly worth it. Value came from first-round independent checks against code or a build; repeated rounds, the auditor and gate reviewing the same draft, per-commit review and mutation on type-only modules were waste; no reviewer caught a logic bug (28% of human-found findings); 77% of subagent tokens went to ad hoc general-purpose agents and forks, not plugins; plugin agents mostly ran without their skills. The second half of the catch-rate report was reconstructed from the agent's notes, so its exact counts are approximate.
201	
202	Changed (ADR 015): two rounds for every exit gate and the challenger, escalation on a repeated blocker, hook cap `retry_count` above 1; drafter self-check then gate, with auditor, verifier and architecture audit on request or for shared or cross-module specs; spec gates check claims against their sources; review once per batch; mutation skipped when no executable logic changed. Versions: muse 1.2.0, scribe 3.6.0, smith 2.6.0, navigator 2.5.0, sentinel 2.1.4, ranger 3.2.5, ecosystem 4.6.0.
203	
204	Next: behavior checks for the logic-bug gap; skills as the entry point (routing); collapsing build-side chains; main-loop cost (forks); measure with paired fix-task sequences.
205	
206	Behavior checks and routing (same branch): `shared/references/verification/evidence.md` now says structure is not behavior (run changed logic on representative and edge inputs from the criterion or defect; inspect the built page for visual changes), and the smith reviewer and exit gate, ranger exit gate and sentinel verifier load it. 26 pipeline agents' descriptions now name the skill that starts them; resident agent description text fell from about 3,079 to 2,239 tokens. One live run (Sonnet 5.5, smith plugin, a two-line bug "add(2, 3) returns 6") used no skill or agent: the model fixed it directly and added a test that fails on the original bug. That run does not test routing, because direct work is proportionate for a bug that size; routing needs a multi-file task, measured with the runbook.
207	
208	## Routing: entry commands and the routing guard
209	
210	| Finding | Action | Evidence |
211	| :--- | :--- | :--- |
212	| Sessions called pipeline agents directly (318 agent calls against 12 skill uses in one Callisto session), so skill-level checks never ran; 33 skills named by plugin are hard to pick | New `guide` plugin: `/guide:explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` hand off to the existing skills by risk; an `AGENTS.md` snippet in its README | `just check` |
213	| A prompt cannot force routing; a hook can see it. Traced on Claude Code with a probe plugin: a typed `/plugin:skill` arrives only as a `UserPromptSubmit` prompt, a model-started skill as a `PreToolUse` `Skill` call, a subagent call as a `PreToolUse` `Agent` call with `subagent_type`, all with one `session_id` | `shared/hooks/route-guard.py <plugin>`, registered by muse, navigator, ranger, scribe, sentinel and smith for their own agents: a direct call is denied once per agent per session until one of the plugin's skills has started, then goes through; fails open; `WISP_ROUTE_GUARD=off` disables it | `tests/test_route_guard.py` (6 tests); live run: "have smith:reviewer review calc.py" was denied once with the redirect and the explicit retry went through |
214	
215	Limit, observed live: with `guide` and `smith` loaded, a generic "review my fix before I merge" was handled by the model itself (read, run tests) with no skill or agent, so the guard never fired. The guard stops agents being used without their checks; it does not make the model choose a skill. For that, the levers are the project's `AGENTS.md` (snippet in `plugins/guide/README.md`), typing the `/guide:` commands, and, if measurement shows substantive work still skipping checks, an outcome guard on code changes (not built).
216	
217	
218	## ADR evidence
219	
220	Measurements, counts and limits that were cut from ADRs 011 to 017 when the records were condensed to decision, reasons, rejected alternatives and consequences. Figures already recorded elsewhere in this log are cross-referenced, not repeated.
221	
222	### ADR 011: exploration modes
223	
224	- **Projects and period.** Two real projects, the Orin DX and Techworx sites, September and October 2026.
225	- **Gate cost on component specs.** Eight component specs took 51 gate calls in under an hour. Every one failed its first gate, and the retry cap of 3 was not enforced (see ADR 012 below). The specs described behavior well and appearance not at all, so the owner asked for drawings and rewrote the gated specs the next day.
226	- **Two-phase request.** On 14 October the owner asked to explore quickly first and add specs and tests once ideas narrow. The audit machinery was stopped by hand, and the landing, Tools and Principles pages then took about 30 minutes.
227	- **Where ideation ran.** Almost entirely outside the plugins, in forks and general-purpose agents: about 24.8 million subagent tokens (forks alone), more than all the gates together (muse gates about 8.15 million over 79 calls; `verification/VERIFY-3.md` section 3). Decisions were lost between sessions.
228	- **Skill invocation.** 7 Skill calls in 812 transcripts, so agents reachable only through skills never ran (`investigations/unused-agents.md`; Track D above).
229	- **Gated path on a stable contract.** The SiteNav work passed 478 end-to-end tests, which is why the gates were not loosened for everyone.
230	- **Outside practice.** Vercel's product-design skill routes between a read-only shaping mode and a hardening mode; Anthropic's guidance says exploratory work may skip planning.
231	- **Pilots and limits.** Each mode was piloted once (`investigations/exploration-pilots.md`; Wave 1 above). Whether the light path is chosen when it should be, and whether it speeds exploration without raising later defects, is not measured (`docs/evaluation-methodology.md`). No plugin version or changelog changed when the modes were added.
232	
233	### ADR 012: hook enforcement
234	
235	- **Conformance.** In the two audited projects, 12 of 45 recorded verdicts broke the schema, all 12 by a `verdict_summary` over 300 characters (see "What the work found" above). Eight specs passed their gate with `retry_count` between 4 and 9 (see "Hook enforcement" above). The `muse` gate was told to emit a verdict value that no schema allows (`escalate`).
236	- **Platform.** Claude Code 2.1.271 and later deliver a subagent's report in auto mode through `SubagentHandback`; the report is `tool_input.message`. Recorded in `docs/verified-facts.md`. `onFailure: "block"` needs 2.1.295; the CLI used for the checks was 2.1.292.
237	- **Live run.** On 2026-10-20, `muse:exit-gate` through `claude -p --permission-mode auto`: the hook denied twice and accepted the corrected third report. One run, one gate, one model. The four other gate agents ran in the Gate rounds live runs above.
238	- **Not done.** Codex and Antigravity enforcement; the workflow-script alternative is deferred to WP-603.
239	
240	### ADR 013: round discipline
241	
242	- **Blocker counts.** SPEC-001 went 18, 5, 6, 0, 0, 2, 0, 6, 2, 3, 2, 8, 3 across 13 rounds (see "Gate rounds" above). Eight specs passed only at `retry_count` 4 to 9. A zero followed by a nonzero count means a later round found issues an earlier round could have found, or a fix broke something.
243	- **Cost.** The muse gates cost about 8.15 million tokens over 79 calls (`verification/VERIFY-3.md` section 5; `CATALOG.md`, WP-50 and WP-212).
244	- **Scope of the rule change.** The constitution is copied into all 40 agents then in the tree (45 now), which is why the rule is not placed there.
245	- **Limits.** The live runs confirm the hook fires and the gates produce evidence-citing blockers (round one only); they do not show that rounds fall. Nothing measures the retry rule. The hook cannot distinguish a fix-induced blocker from a late-found one because a retry is a new subagent with no stored prior verdict (the `verdict@4` question, WP-212).
246	
247	### ADR 014: outcome-level plans
248	
249	- **Plan size.** Plans of 60 to 130 KB stalled agents in the audited projects (`ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md`, assumption 10). The planner prompt was the second-largest agent file.
250	- **Fixture.** Old planner 9,777 characters, new 5,578 (43% smaller), both valid against `plan@1` with all six criteria covered (see "Outcome-level plans" above). One run each on one small fixture.
251	- **Not tested.** Whether implementers do better or worse from outcome-level plans, and the challenger on either shape.
252	- **Schema.** Required task fields are `id`, `title`, `files`, `steps` and `commit_message`; "exact code" appears only in a field description, and `additionalProperties` is false. The stale descriptions are left because a published schema is immutable.
253	
254	### ADR 015: two rounds and one check against reality
255	
256	- **Sources.** Documented evaluations; session token data over 1,555 subagent calls and 253 million reported tokens in five projects; reviewer catch rate over about 400 runs (summary under "Evidence review and ADR 015" above). The second half of the catch-rate report was reconstructed from the agent's notes, so its exact counts are approximate; the direction is supported independently by the gate-round records and the session data.
257	- **First-round catches.** A spec criterion pointing attestation at the wrong commit; an `init` that writes a config the loader rejects; a plan diagnostic that could never fire; padding that computed to zero in the built page.
258	- **Long loops.** One implementation gate ran 14 rounds after calling the code correct in round 3; one plan ran 29 challenge rounds; one spec ran 13 gate rounds with blockers returning after clean rounds. Reviewers ran per commit with no logic bug caught, and mutation ran on modules with no executable logic.
259	- **Hook cap.** Before this record the hook allowed three retries; it now denies a fail at `retry_count` 1 without `escalation_required`.
260	- **Not measured.** The effect of the change; use the paired fix-task sequences in `docs/evaluation-runbook.md`. Logic bugs (28% of human-found findings) need behavior checks (`shared/references/verification/evidence.md`).
261	
262	### ADR 016: spec unknowns
263	
264	- **Before.** The drafters and gates (`scribe`, `muse`) failed a spec for any TBD "regardless of how minor", and the gate-readiness checklist sent every unknown to `non_goals` or `reasoning`.
265	- **Reach of a `spec@2`.** `spec@1` is named in more than 70 authored files across seven plugins, the Codex skills and the pipeline fixtures.
266	- **Not measured.** Whether gate rounds and rewrites fall; compare gate rounds per spec before and after with `docs/evaluation-runbook.md`.
267	
268	### ADR 017: dropping `<backstory>`
269	
270	- **Population.** 44 agents carried a backstory; 43 only restated the goal or judgment, and one (`weaver:intake`) needed a sentence moved into `<judgment>`.
271	- **Ablation design.** Paired, 5 runs per condition on seeded defects, with and without the backstory, on `scribe:exit-gate`, `navigator:challenger` and `courier:changeset-analyzer` (Sonnet 5.5), scored on each agent's own output.
272	- **Catch rate.** Every seeded defect was found in 5 of 5 runs in both conditions. Gate: an untestable criterion, a criterion contradicting the code, a missing out-of-range case, a fail verdict. Challenger: an uncovered criterion, a wrong task order. Analyzer: a link, a direct-push limit, a bold lead-in, a disposition, a semver impact, a scripting field.
273	- **Size and cost (median per run, with backstory then without).** Gate 10,346 characters and $0.32, then 10,499 and $0.31. Challenger 6,039 and $0.19, then 6,023 and $0.18. Analyzer 6,621 and $0.23, then 6,359 and $0.23.
274	- **Limits.** The seeded defects were easy, so every run hit the ceiling and the test could not show a backstory helping; three agents of 44, one model, 5 runs each. It shows no measurable effect, not that there is none. Per-run outputs were not kept.

Status as of 2026-10-20 on branch `worktree-frontend-design-evaluation`. Five of the Wave 0 work packages in `CATALOG.md` are started or done. Nothing is released: no plugin version, changelog or tag changed (see "Release bookkeeping").

| WP | Status | What changed | Verified by |

| WP-620 Claude manifests | Done | `tools/sync-claude-manifests.py` generates `plugins/<id>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (name, version, description, author) from each `plugin.json`, with `--check`; `just claude-manifests` is in `just check` and CI; `just claude-validate` runs `claude plugin validate --strict` on every plugin and the marketplace | `just claude-validate`: 10 plugins and the marketplace pass `--strict`, and validation now reads each manifest (before, the directory form checked nothing) |
| WP-622 AGY and root marketplace | Partly done | Removed the dead `$schema` URL (404) from the root `marketplace.json`; nothing in tests, scripts or CI read it | `just check` |
| WP-624 Hook validator spike | Done, registered | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py`, a `PreToolUse` hook on `SubagentHandback` that checks exit-gate handbacks against their verdict schema, denies with the errors, caps denials at 3 per agent, enforces the retry cap in the report, and fails open; registered by `hooks/hooks.json` in muse, scribe, smith, sentinel and ranger (ADR 012) | `tests/test_handback_validator.py` (13 tests) and a live run and `verification/scripts/handback-conformance.py` over 45 recorded verdicts |
| WP-01 and WP-02 `muse` fixes | Done | The `muse` docs no longer point to a ranger accessibility taxonomy that does not exist (`plugin.json`, README, `SKILL.md`, root `marketplace.json`); the `muse` exit-gate produces `verdict@3` (agent, skill, README, `plugin.json`, Codex skill and catalog, root README table); `verdict@1` has no producer and is kept unchanged | `just check` (66 tests); `just marketplace-check`; validator tests for `muse` routing and for escalation as a blocker |

## What the work found

- **`claude plugin validate plugins/<id>` was a false pass** because the manifests sit at the plugin root. With the generated `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` it validates the manifest, and the repo-only keys (`id`, `consumes`, `produces`) stay in `plugin.json` where Claude Code ignores them.
- **Recorded gate verdicts nearly all conform to their schemas.** 33 of 45 conform; all 12 violations are `verdict_summary` over 300 characters (`VERIFY-3.md` section 5). A hook would have asked for one trim on about 27% of handbacks.
- **`muse` gates mostly emitted `verdict@3`-shaped output** (26 of 36; the other 9 of the 45 files are `scribe` gates) while `muse` documented `verdict@1`, and its prompt told the agent to set `verdict` to `"escalate"`, which no schema allows. WP-02 (done) moved `muse` to `verdict@3` and made escalation an `escalation_required` blocker, as in the other four gates; the validator now checks `muse` against `verdict@3` only.
- **A bug in the validator was found only by real data:** a schema property with a list of types (`["string", "null"]`). It is fixed and has a regression test.
- **The `requirement@1` schema describes `reasoning` as "chain-of-thought during capture".** It is immutable (ADR 004), agents reach it through a file read and not a prompt, so the lint carries a documented exception; a future `requirement@2` should use the "private scratchpad" wording.

## Open items from this work

- The README documents AGY installs through the community `agy-plugins-cli`. Fetched source snippets suggest that tool discovers plugins as top-level repository directories, which would not find plugins under `plugins/`. This is unverified; test an install in an isolated environment before changing the README (WP-622, WP-621).
- The installed plugins use `shared -> ../../shared` symlinks and the Claude marketplace installs from the `plugins/<id>` subdirectory (`git-subdir`). Whether the symlink resolves after install is untested (WP-621).
- The hook is a spike: it needs a plugin `hooks/hooks.json` registration, a decision on how it is distributed (the tool lives outside any plugin directory), and a check against a live gate agent in auto mode before WP-602 builds on it.
- Hook behavior on Claude Code 2.1.292: `onFailure: "block"` needs 2.1.295, so a crashing hook does not block (the validator fails open by design).

## Change record (shared/harness-authoring.md)

```text
Classification: Codex workflow (role-card resource), distribution (generated bundle), shared identity (Claude manifest generation, root marketplace)
Counterpart reviewed: plugins/*/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, harnesses/codex/agent-roles/README.md, shared/harness-authoring.md, docs/codex-marketplace-release-policy.md
Intent preserved: role boundaries and the delegation packet are unchanged; only model ids and a freshness note changed. Plugin identity (id, version, author, consumes, produces) is unchanged and still authoritative in plugins/<id>/plugin.json.
Intentional divergence: Claude Code reads .claude-plugin/plugin.json, so a generated minimal manifest sits beside the repo manifest; Codex tiers were re-chosen by position (luna, sol, astra) and are explicitly unevaluated.
Codex role impact: model ids in all ten materialized agent-roles/README.md files; no skill changes.
Verification: just check; just claude-validate; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests; scripts under docs/evaluations/frontend-design/verification/scripts
```

## Release bookkeeping not done

The repo's contribution checklist asks for a plugin version bump, a plugin changelog entry and a matching marketplace entry when a plugin's behavior changes, and the version check compares all of them. These changes touch every plugin's packaged files (the Codex role README, a new Claude manifest), so a release would bump all ten plugins and the ecosystem version together. That is a release decision, so no version, changelog or tag was changed. Until then `just versions` passes because nothing it compares moved, and the generated Claude manifests copy whatever version `plugin.json` has.

## Second pass (Wave 0 completion)

| WP-05 repo claims | Done | The README and `ARCHITECTURE.md` counts (ten plugins, 44 agents, 30 skills, 31 schemas) were checked and are accurate | none |

Live run: `courier:changeset-analyzer` on `gh pr diff 483 --repo orin-dx/callisto` (24.9 kB), one run on Sonnet 5.5. It returned one `new` entry for one outcome: a lead line on the link, then what you see and where, the limit that a changeset pushed straight to the branch gets no link, the optional `pr` field for scripts, and that upgrading needs no action. It classified the change as a minor new capability. It did not write the "why it helps" as a separate bullet but put it in the lead line.

**Finding: `shared/...` reference paths depend on the working directory.** In that run the agent reported it could not find `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` and fell back to the schema-implied rules. This is separate from, and in addition to, the dangling-symlink install defect fixed in the marketplace sources (VERIFY-3 section 7): even a correct install leaves a relative `shared/...` path unresolvable from a user's project. It likely explains the pilots where schema files were not readable at run time. Not fixed here. `pr-narrator` and `commit-analyzer` were then changed to match: they follow the repository's own conventions (a pull request template, recent commit scopes and subject style), keep limits in the body instead of the scratchpad, mark breaking changes to command output, exit codes and file formats, and the narrator names or recommends a changeset. ## Model and effort fit

Audit of all 45 agents against the constitution's tiers (haiku/low for mechanical work, sonnet/medium for analysis and execution, opus/high for binding judgment). Two clear mismatches changed: `courier:release-summarizer` sonnet/medium to haiku/low (deterministic aggregation), `scribe:drift-checker` opus/high to sonnet/medium (a diagnostic, not a gate). Left alone pending measurement, in order of likely saving: `ranger:adversary` (one opus call per candidate), `scribe:arch-auditor` (opus on every spec), `sentinel:exit-gate` (maps a verifier report to a verdict without re-reading evidence, so it may not need opus), and whether opus gates need `high` rather than the default effort. Gate quality decides retry rounds, so a cheaper gate that misses more can cost more than it saves; test with the spec-gating comparison in `docs/evaluation-runbook.md` before changing them.

## Evidence review and ADR 015

Three independent reads (documented evidence; session token data over 1,555 subagent calls and 253M reported tokens in five projects; reviewer catch rate over about 400 runs) agreed the structure is partly worth it. Value came from first-round independent checks against code or a build; repeated rounds, the auditor and gate reviewing the same draft, per-commit review and mutation on type-only modules were waste; no reviewer caught a logic bug (28% of human-found findings); 77% of subagent tokens went to ad hoc general-purpose agents and forks, not plugins; plugin agents mostly ran without their skills. The second half of the catch-rate report was reconstructed from the agent's notes, so its exact counts are approximate.

Changed (ADR 015): two rounds for every exit gate and the challenger, escalation on a repeated blocker, hook cap `retry_count` above 1; drafter self-check then gate, with auditor, verifier and architecture audit on request or for shared or cross-module specs; spec gates check claims against their sources; review once per batch; mutation skipped when no executable logic changed. Versions: muse 1.2.0, scribe 3.6.0, smith 2.6.0, navigator 2.5.0, sentinel 2.1.4, ranger 3.2.5, ecosystem 4.6.0.

Next: behavior checks for the logic-bug gap; skills as the entry point (routing); collapsing build-side chains; main-loop cost (forks); measure with paired fix-task sequences.

Behavior checks and routing (same branch): `shared/references/verification/evidence.md` now says structure is not behavior (run changed logic on representative and edge inputs from the criterion or defect; inspect the built page for visual changes), and the smith reviewer and exit gate, ranger exit gate and sentinel verifier load it. 26 pipeline agents' descriptions now name the skill that starts them; resident agent description text fell from about 3,079 to 2,239 tokens. One live run (Sonnet 5.5, smith plugin, a two-line bug "add(2, 3) returns 6") used no skill or agent: the model fixed it directly and added a test that fails on the original bug. That run does not test routing, because direct work is proportionate for a bug that size; routing needs a multi-file task, measured with the runbook.

## ADR evidence

Measurements, counts and limits that were cut from ADRs 011 to 017 when the records were condensed to decision, reasons, rejected alternatives and consequences. Figures already recorded elsewhere in this log are cross-referenced, not repeated.

### ADR 011: exploration modes

- **Projects and period.** Two real projects, the Orin DX and Techworx sites, September and October 2026.
- **Gate cost on component specs.** Eight component specs took 51 gate calls in under an hour. Every one failed its first gate, and the retry cap of 3 was not enforced (see ADR 012 below). The specs described behavior well and appearance not at all, so the owner asked for drawings and rewrote the gated specs the next day.
- **Two-phase request.** On 14 October the owner asked to explore quickly first and add specs and tests once ideas narrow. The audit machinery was stopped by hand, and the landing, Tools and Principles pages then took about 30 minutes.
- **Where ideation ran.** Almost entirely outside the plugins, in forks and general-purpose agents: about 24.8 million subagent tokens (forks alone), more than all the gates together (muse gates about 8.15 million over 79 calls; `verification/VERIFY-3.md` section 3). Decisions were lost between sessions.
- **Skill invocation.** 7 Skill calls in 812 transcripts, so agents reachable only through skills never ran (`investigations/unused-agents.md`; Track D above).
- **Gated path on a stable contract.** The SiteNav work passed 478 end-to-end tests, which is why the gates were not loosened for everyone.
- **Outside practice.** Vercel's product-design skill routes between a read-only shaping mode and a hardening mode; Anthropic's guidance says exploratory work may skip planning.
- **Pilots and limits.** Each mode was piloted once (`investigations/exploration-pilots.md`; Wave 1 above). Whether the light path is chosen when it should be, and whether it speeds exploration without raising later defects, is not measured (`docs/evaluation-methodology.md`). No plugin version or changelog changed when the modes were added.

### ADR 012: hook enforcement

- **Conformance.** In the two audited projects, 12 of 45 recorded verdicts broke the schema, all 12 by a `verdict_summary` over 300 characters (see "What the work found" above). Eight specs passed their gate with `retry_count` between 4 and 9 (see "Hook enforcement" above). The `muse` gate was told to emit a verdict value that no schema allows (`escalate`).
- **Platform.** Claude Code 2.1.271 and later deliver a subagent's report in auto mode through `SubagentHandback`; the report is `tool_input.message`. Recorded in `docs/verified-facts.md`. `onFailure: "block"` needs 2.1.295; the CLI used for the checks was 2.1.292.
- **Live run.** On 2026-10-20, `muse:exit-gate` through `claude -p --permission-mode auto`: the hook denied twice and accepted the corrected third report. One run, one gate, one model. The four other gate agents ran in the Gate rounds live runs above.
- **Not done.** Codex and Antigravity enforcement; the workflow-script alternative is deferred to WP-603.

### ADR 013: round discipline

- **Blocker counts.** SPEC-001 went 18, 5, 6, 0, 0, 2, 0, 6, 2, 3, 2, 8, 3 across 13 rounds (see "Gate rounds" above). Eight specs passed only at `retry_count` 4 to 9. A zero followed by a nonzero count means a later round found issues an earlier round could have found, or a fix broke something.
- **Cost.** The muse gates cost about 8.15 million tokens over 79 calls (`verification/VERIFY-3.md` section 5; `CATALOG.md`, WP-50 and WP-212).
- **Scope of the rule change.** The constitution is copied into all 40 agents then in the tree (45 now), which is why the rule is not placed there.
- **Limits.** The live runs confirm the hook fires and the gates produce evidence-citing blockers (round one only); they do not show that rounds fall. Nothing measures the retry rule. The hook cannot distinguish a fix-induced blocker from a late-found one because a retry is a new subagent with no stored prior verdict (the `verdict@4` question, WP-212).

### ADR 014: outcome-level plans

- **Plan size.** Plans of 60 to 130 KB stalled agents in the audited projects (`ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md`, assumption 10). The planner prompt was the second-largest agent file.
- **Fixture.** Old planner 9,777 characters, new 5,578 (43% smaller), both valid against `plan@1` with all six criteria covered (see "Outcome-level plans" above). One run each on one small fixture.
- **Not tested.** Whether implementers do better or worse from outcome-level plans, and the challenger on either shape.
- **Schema.** Required task fields are `id`, `title`, `files`, `steps` and `commit_message`; "exact code" appears only in a field description, and `additionalProperties` is false. The stale descriptions are left because a published schema is immutable.

### ADR 015: two rounds and one check against reality

- **Sources.** Documented evaluations; session token data over 1,555 subagent calls and 253 million reported tokens in five projects; reviewer catch rate over about 400 runs (summary under "Evidence review and ADR 015" above). The second half of the catch-rate report was reconstructed from the agent's notes, so its exact counts are approximate; the direction is supported independently by the gate-round records and the session data.
- **First-round catches.** A spec criterion pointing attestation at the wrong commit; an `init` that writes a config the loader rejects; a plan diagnostic that could never fire; padding that computed to zero in the built page.
- **Long loops.** One implementation gate ran 14 rounds after calling the code correct in round 3; one plan ran 29 challenge rounds; one spec ran 13 gate rounds with blockers returning after clean rounds. Reviewers ran per commit with no logic bug caught, and mutation ran on modules with no executable logic.
- **Hook cap.** Before this record the hook allowed three retries; it now denies a fail at `retry_count` 1 without `escalation_required`.
- **Not measured.** The effect of the change; use the paired fix-task sequences in `docs/evaluation-runbook.md`. Logic bugs (28% of human-found findings) need behavior checks (`shared/references/verification/evidence.md`).

### ADR 016: spec unknowns

- **Before.** The drafters and gates (`scribe`, `muse`) failed a spec for any TBD "regardless of how minor", and the gate-readiness checklist sent every unknown to `non_goals` or `reasoning`.
- **Reach of a `spec@2`.** `spec@1` is named in more than 70 authored files across seven plugins, the Codex skills and the pipeline fixtures.
- **Not measured.** Whether gate rounds and rewrites fall; compare gate rounds per spec before and after with `docs/evaluation-runbook.md`.

### ADR 017: dropping `<backstory>`

- **Population.** 44 agents carried a backstory; 43 only restated the goal or judgment, and one (`weaver:intake`) needed a sentence moved into `<judgment>`.
- **Ablation design.** Paired, 5 runs per condition on seeded defects, with and without the backstory, on `scribe:exit-gate`, `navigator:challenger` and `courier:changeset-analyzer` (Sonnet 5.5), scored on each agent's own output.
- **Catch rate.** Every seeded defect was found in 5 of 5 runs in both conditions. Gate: an untestable criterion, a criterion contradicting the code, a missing out-of-range case, a fail verdict. Challenger: an uncovered criterion, a wrong task order. Analyzer: a link, a direct-push limit, a bold lead-in, a disposition, a semver impact, a scripting field.
- **Size and cost (median per run, with backstory then without).** Gate 10,346 characters and $0.32, then 10,499 and $0.31. Challenger 6,039 and $0.19, then 6,023 and $0.18. Analyzer 6,621 and $0.23, then 6,359 and $0.23.
- **Limits.** The seeded defects were easy, so every run hit the ceiling and the test could not show a backstory helping; three agents of 44, one model, 5 runs each. It shows no measurable effect, not that there is none. Per-run outputs were not kept.

# Architecture review against current agent capabilities

Status: proposal, revised after primary-source verification (section 7.1 and `verification/Y1` to `Y6`, `VERIFY-3`). Nothing here changes a plugin, schema, constitution or ADR. It tests each architectural assumption in `ARCHITECTURE.md` against what the current agent platforms can do, and adds the work packages that follow (WP-601 to WP-616 first, WP-617 to WP-628 after verification; 172 in total with the catalog's 144). Where section 7.1 and an earlier row differ, 7.1 wins.

Inputs: `ARCHITECTURE.md`; `evidence/Z1-claude-platform.md` (Claude Code and Anthropic engineering guidance); `evidence/Z2-other-harnesses.md` (Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, Copilot, standards); repo measurements taken for this review (section 1). Claims tagged [P] were read on a primary page, [S] come from a search summary, [I] are inference. Z1 read only the first 100k characters of the hooks and subagents pages, and the fetch tool summarizes pages, so quotes are the fetcher's wording.

## 0. Corrections to earlier statements

1. **The constitution is not 290 lines per agent.** Every one of the 44 agents embeds the same 6-line `<constitution>` block (one distinct block, checked by hash). The 290-line `shared/constitution.md` is the authoring-time rulebook; among agents only the `mason` auditor reads it at runtime. The research notes and `traceability/MAP-5-M-X.md` assumed a 290-line copy per agent, and so did my earlier summaries. The per-agent cost is about 6 lines. This lowers the priority of the "shrink the constitution" ablation (WP-62, ADR N10). See section 2, row 3.
2. **Cross-harness shape (from the user).** Codex has its own native plugin format, set up in this repo under `harnesses/codex/`; AGY's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree. The cost is therefore one authored tree for Claude and AGY plus one native Codex tree, not three. The AGY risks are specific (section 6), not a third tree.
3. **Agent descriptions are inside the platform's budget.** Descriptions across the 44 agents total 26,908 characters, about 6.7k tokens by a 4-characters-per-token estimate, against a 15,000-token cap on all agent descriptions [P per Z1]. That is about 45% of the cap. There is headroom, but every agent added (the structure decision proposes 3) draws on the same budget, so keep descriptions short.

## 1. Where the repo stands (measured)

| Fact | Value |
| :-- | :-- |
| Plugins / skills / agents | 10 / 30 / 44 |
| Agent frontmatter keys in use | `name`, `role`, `model`, `effort`, `description` only. No `tools`, `maxTurns`, `isolation`, `skills`, `memory` or other native controls |
| Tier distribution | sonnet/medium 27, opus/high 8, haiku/low 7, `claude-fable-5-1`/high 2 |
| Skill frontmatter keys | `name`, `description`, `version` |
| Plugin-shipped hooks, `bin/` validators, workflows, LSP servers | none (the repo has a commit-time integrity hook for its own development only) |
| Distinct `<constitution>` blocks across agents | 1 (6 lines) |
| Average agent body | about 4.4k characters |
| Orchestration | skill prompts that spawn subagents; retry counter lives in `verdict@3` and is incremented by the exit-gate agent |

## 2. Assumption ledger

Verdicts: **Keep**, **Change**, **Test first** (evidence is mixed; measure before deciding), **Lower priority**.

| # | Assumption (where it lives) | What current platforms and evidence say | Verdict | Work |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 1 | Context is scarce; load references on demand (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 1) | Skills are progressive disclosure natively; Anthropic's context-engineering guidance asks for the minimal information that fully outlines behavior [P per Z1]. Subagent frontmatter can preload skills | **Keep** | WP-606 (use native preload where it helps) |
| 2 | One agent per cognitive mode (ADR 003) | Anthropic's guide calls splitting by role (planner, implementer, tester, reviewer) an anti-pattern and recommends splitting by *context* [P per Z1]. Verifier and adversary splits are justified by independent context. Multi-agent runs cost about 15x chat tokens in one post and 3 to 10x single-agent in a later guide; it underperforms on tightly coupled work, "most coding tasks" included. A multi-agent research setup beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal eval. No vendor test of 40-plus role agents in a linear pipeline exists | **Test first** | WP-605, WP-601 |
| 3 | A byte-identical constitution is the shared cache prefix (ADR 006) | The block is only 6 lines, so its cost is small whatever it saves. Cache prefixes are shared only between requests with the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and working directory, and subagent caches default to a 5-minute TTL [P per Z1], so the cache benefit across 44 differently configured agents is probably small [I]. The drift guard (byte-identity check) already exists | **Lower priority** | WP-62 retargets to backstory and skeleton; WP-604 only measures |
| 4 | Capability tiers by model and effort (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5) | Effort is a native per-agent control; defaults differ by model (Fable 5.1 high, Opus 5.5 medium, Sonnet 5.5 high on the API, Haiku 5.5 medium); Opus 5.5 at medium roughly matches Opus 5 at high per Anthropic. Pricing per million tokens: Fable 5.1 $10/$50, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10 [P per Z1]. Two agents already run on Fable 5.1 | **Keep as hints; re-measure** | WP-63 |
| 5 | JSON schemas are the inter-agent contract, with a mandatory `reasoning` scratchpad (ADR 004) | Schemas remain the portable contract across harnesses. Workflow scripts can pass a JSON schema to `agent()` with validation retries, and a `SubagentStop` hook can run a validator [P per Z1]. Anthropic names a `reasoning` field as a refusal trigger; first-hand (`VERIFY-3`): the real drafter prompt with its scratchpad field completed normally twice, only a demand for verbatim reasoning was refused, and 72k+ transcript messages show no refusals | **Keep schemas; change enforcement; test the field first** | WP-602, WP-61 |
| 6 | Default-fail gates with a retry cap of 3, then a human (`ARCHITECTURE.md` section 6) | The gate concept is a differentiator no harness provides natively (section 5). But a prompt-based gate is only a request: in the `pages` session the cap was not enforced. Anthropic's harness post says evaluators drift lenient and the multi-agent guide names the "early victory problem"; VISTA found 8.3% of agents claiming success despite failed checks [P abstract per Z2]. `Stop`, `SubagentStop` and `TaskCompleted` hooks can block with a reason, and the hook can hold a counter a model cannot reliably keep | **Keep the gate; make it deterministic** | WP-602 |
| 7 | Orchestration is a skill prompt that spawns subagents | Every result lands in the orchestrator's context. Plugins can ship workflow scripts (`agent()`, `pipeline()`, `parallel()`) that keep state outside the model, are resumable, and allow 16 concurrent agents and 1,000 agents per run [P per Z1]; they run in the CLI, headless mode and the SDK. Not portable: Antigravity workflows stop on 2026-10-19 [S per Z2], and Codex has no equivalent plugin construct | **Change on Claude; keep the skill as the cross-harness path** | WP-603 |
| 8 | Work is a sequential pipeline of ten plugins | Testimonials (not controlled benchmarks) report 18-plus-hour unattended runs on Opus 5.5 and a 38-hour run on Fable 5.1 [P per Z1]; Anthropic's harness post reports a simplified harness (sprint construct removed; planner and evaluator kept) at 3h50m and $124.70 on Opus 4.6, against an earlier 6h/$200 run on Opus 4.5 with a different prompt; it is not a before/after on one task and was not re-checked on 5.x. Stage granularity tuned for short horizons will not stay right | **Change: make stages elidable, gates at boundaries** | WP-608, WP-18 |
| 9 | Plans carry exact implementation code (navigator, ADR 009) | Anthropic says prescriptive skills "can degrade output quality" on Fable 5 [P]; plans of 60 to 130 KB stalled agents in the sessions (VERIFY-1: 17 failed tasks in the `orin-dx` session) | **Change: outcome-level plans** | WP-608, WP-36 |
| 10 | Verification evidence is text, code and tests; "render" is only a label | Browser capture is native in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Cursor [S for most]; VISTA found 44.5% of trajectories never looked at the design screenshots and 73% skipped prescribed self-audits | **Change** | WP-607 |
| 11 | Agents are stateless across sessions | Subagents can have persistent `memory`; plugins have a persistent data directory; routines and scheduled runs exist [P per Z1] | **Change** | WP-612 |
| 12 | One lifecycle contract, two source trees | Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (2026-08-06) standardizes the portable core (root `plugin.json`, `skills/`, `mcp.json`) and excludes hooks, commands, agents, marketplaces and permissions [P per Z2]. Claude Code and AGY are not named in it; AGY's plugin format is similar to Claude's | **Keep two trees; narrow the duplication** | WP-610 |
| 13 | Humans approve through written artifacts | Rendered review surfaces exist (Artifacts, MCP Apps, Claude Design handoff); the user asked for pictures repeatedly | **Change** | WP-614, WP-34 |
| 14 | Agents use platform controls only through `model` and `effort` | Native controls available: `tools` allowlists, `maxTurns`, `isolation: worktree`, `skills` preload, `memory`, `omitClaudeMd`. Plugin-shipped agents ignore `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `permissionMode` [P per Z1] | **Change** | WP-606, WP-615 |

## 3. What the harnesses do natively and what we re-implement

| Capability | Native | In this repo today | Call |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Parallel agents and worktrees | Claude `isolation: worktree`; Codex managed worktrees (CLI 0.162.0); Antigravity parallel agents | File ownership is prose in plans; no worktree isolation | Adopt natively (WP-606, WP-55) |
| Browser capture and screenshots | Claude built-in browser and Chrome extension; Codex in-app browser; Antigravity browser subagent with Artifacts; Cursor browser | None | Capability-detected adapters (WP-607) |
| Plugin evals with a no-plugin baseline | `claude plugin eval` runs each case 3 times with and 3 without the plugin [P per Z1] | `mason:evaluate` with hidden-oracle fixtures | Complementary: native gives the baseline, ours gives cross-harness fixtures (WP-601) |
| Deterministic gates | Hooks (33 events on Claude [P]; 12 events on Codex [P]; `hooks.json` in AGY plugins) | One repo-level commit hook; none shipped in plugins | Adopt (WP-602) |
| Orchestration scripts | Claude workflow scripts; Codex Agents SDK | Skill prompts | Adopt on Claude (WP-603) |
| Review bots and plan artifacts | Cursor Bugbot, Copilot review, Antigravity plan Artifacts | `ranger`, `sentinel`, `navigator` | Keep; ours add refutation and falsifiable gates |
| Code intelligence | LSP servers can be bundled in Claude plugins [P per Z1]; Netflix and JetBrains report 20 to 30% efficiency gains for Java | Language-service guidance in smith (commit `f10e6b8`) | Extend to UI facts (WP-611) |

## 4. Platform features this repo does not use yet

Plugin-level hooks as gates; `claude plugin eval` with a no-plugin baseline; plugin-shipped workflows; `bin/` validators; `SendMessage` resume for repair loops; `isolation: worktree`; per-agent `maxTurns` as a stall guard; `tools` allowlists; `skills` preload; subagent `memory` and a persistent plugin data directory for counters; plugin `dependencies`; routines for drift checks; bundled LSP servers.

## 5. Differentiators to protect

The harnesses natively do parallel agents, worktrees, browser capture, plan artifacts and review bots. None of them provides falsifiable specs, adversarial refutation, fail-by-default binding gates, or enforced self-audit [S per Z2]. These are why the plugins exist. The direction below moves the *enforcement* of those properties out of prose and into deterministic harness features, and leaves the properties themselves unchanged.

## 6. Direction: thinner prompts, thicker harness

1. **Move enforcement out of prose.** Retry caps, schema validity, "no pass without evidence refs" and self-audit become hook- or workflow-enforced where the harness allows, with the prompt-only path as the cross-harness fallback.
2. **Split agents by context, not by role.** Keep splits that buy independent or high-volume context (verifier, adversary, recon). Audit the rest against that criterion with a measured baseline.
3. **Design for longer autonomy.** Plans state outcomes, ownership and verification; progress is a resumable artifact; gates sit at boundaries, not inside every step.
4. **Make capabilities pluggable and detected.** Browser, worktree, memory and design-source access are adapters selected by capability, with identical artifacts out (`render-evidence`, `design-source`).
5. **Keep schemas as the cross-harness contract,** and share skill bodies where orchestration semantics are identical.
6. **Record the assumptions.** A register of what each component assumes the model cannot do, reviewed on each model generation (WP-609), so stale scaffolding is retired on evidence.

Cross-harness specifics:
- **Codex:** native plugin format under `harnesses/codex/`; custom agents are natively TOML [P], and this repo's policy keeps role cards as markdown resources (ADR N8 decides whether an optional generator may emit TOML). Subagents spawn only when asked or when a skill or AGENTS.md instructs it, so Codex orchestrator skills must say so. Re-check the generated tree against the new `extensions.com.openai` convention [P per Z2].
- **AGY:** plugin fields `plugin.json` (with `$schema`), optional `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `rules/`; workflows are not supported in plugins and stop working on 2026-10-19 [S], so author skills only. The public docs do not document the third-party marketplace schema, so the `$schema` reference in the root `marketplace.json` needs re-verifying [P per Z2]. Gemini CLI was retired in June [S].

## 6. Direction: thinner prompts, thicker harness
